violations.description: sha256Hex (createHash('sha256').update(x).digest('hex')) is defined identically three times across files newly added in this same diff: run-synthetic.ts:75, stub-upstream.ts:22, and (via a local sha256Hex used by uuidFromSeed) session-turns.ts:42. All three are byte-identical and directly reusable with no modification. Trivial (2-line) wrapper around a stdlib call, so not blocking, but worth consolidating into one test/e2e-local helper (e.g. test/e2e/hash.ts) since the duplication is entirely within files this PR itself introduced.

sendJson(res, statusCode, body) in stub-upstream.ts is line-for-line identical to src/server.ts:39's sendJson. readRequestBody in stub-upstream.ts (line 150) is a near-duplicate of src/server.ts:53's readRequestBody, minus the maxBodyBytes cap. Not flagged as blocking: stub-upstream.ts is deliberately playing the role of an independent external API double, and importing helpers from src/server.ts (the module under test) would couple the test double to the implementation it's meant to be independent of — the current duplication is probably the architecturally correct choice, not an oversight. Noted for awareness only.

tsconfig.json and tsconfig.build.json now duplicate the entire compilerOptions block verbatim instead of tsconfig.build.json extending tsconfig.json (or both extending a local tsconfig.base.json). This replaces the previous single point of duplication (both extending a since-removed monorepo-relative ../../tsconfig.base.json) with a two-copy inline duplication. Likely an acceptable/necessary fix for this now-standalone package, but flagging since any future compiler-option change now needs to be applied in both files by hand.

notes: run-synthetic.ts's direct console.log/console.error use (vs. cli.ts's injectable io.stdout/io.stderr) is NOT flagged as a violation. cli.ts's injectable IO exists specifically so test/standalone.test.ts can call run(argv, io) in-process and assert on captured output without spawning a subprocess. run-synthetic.ts has no equivalent caller needing to inspect its console output in-process — it's invoked only as a standalone script (package.json's e2e:synthetic), and its actual contract/output is the JSON file it writes (test/e2e/results/synthetic.json), not stdout. src/server.ts itself also uses console.error directly (not injectable IO), confirming injectable IO is a cli.ts-specific pattern tied to its own test coverage, not a codebase-wide rule that run-synthetic.ts breaks.

Layer ownership, coupling, and circular-import checks found no issues: all new test/e2e imports point at legitimate src/ production surfaces (createProxyServer, TelemetryStore, config/types) with no reverse imports from src/ into test/, and no cycles.
Naming and export conventions (named exports throughout, throw new Error(...) for invariant violations, no default exports) are consistent with existing src/presets.ts and src/server.ts precedent.

test/standalone.test.ts (pre-existing) already builds ad hoc inline HTTP stub servers per test file rather than a shared module, so stub-upstream.ts's separate/independent implementation is consistent with established precedent, not a new pattern.
